doc.title: Bob Havens interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Residuals and the union
summary: Residuals from the Welk corporation and the union agreement of the early 1960s.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Do you get any residuals or anything from all those years on TV?
Yes. All of the members that were involved in the original television production receive residuals from the Welk Corporation.
The musician’s union was fairly strong in their influence?

The residual idea I think started in the early 60s, something like that. Anything on television that was before oh about 1961 or 2 I guess, there’s no residuals involved. So that’s why you see a lot of those old shows that date way back. Because they don’t have to deal with the residuals. But we were fortunate and started at a time where this agreement had already been struck with the union, and so we do get the re-run money from that.
